ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based Politically Exposed Person (PEP) screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC guidance, OFAC sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and proprietary commercial screening databases such as World-Check, Dow Jones, or LexisNexis; adverse hits require documented enhanced due diligence, beneficial ownership re-verification, and escalation to the compliance officer before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry operated by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names under the Alberta Business Corporations Act must be in Latin script, incorporate a recognized legal element, and be distinguishable from existing registered names and reserved names; NUANS name search applies standard English/French linguistic transposition and visual/phonetic equivalency analysis, requiring transliteration of non-Latin scripts into official Latin-script form for conflict assessment.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a corporate name search rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registries with a rebuttal statement, formal comparison evidence, and written consent from any conflicting registrant; a further administrative appeal may be brought before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days of the written rejection; alternative name reservations may be filed concurrently to preserve pipeline timing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable under the Alberta Business Corporations Act only if the virtual office provider supplies a physical street address within Alberta, consents to service of process, and maintains mail forwarding capacity; a post office box alone is prohibited; CRA may nonetheless assess whether the virtual office constitutes a place of business for GST/HST, Canada-US treaty, and permanent establishment purposes, but such an arrangement does not by itself prevent incorporation of the Ontario-based factory inspection agency.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 2-5% annual probability for a low-risk testing, inspection and quality-control agency); Alberta Corporate Registry does not conduct routine physical premises inspections; CRA may conduct books-and-records audits; ISO/IEC 17020 or client-mandated supplier audits may occur but are contractual, not statutory; no unannounced regulatory factory inspection is anticipated under ISIC 7120.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss. 7, 8, 12, 23-24, 102-115; Alta Reg 55/2009; alternative federal statute: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta (Edmonton/Calgary counters and online portals)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (prescribed Alberta corporate form under Alta Reg 55/2009)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow deposit or capital bank-account requirement for non-offering private corporations; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration determined by directors under ABCA s. 25
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED by the sole subscriber/director as the First Resolution of [Company Name]: (1) The allotment and subscription of [N] Class A common shares be and is hereby accepted, receipt of lawful consideration duly acknowledged; (2) Shares shall be entered in the share register, and certificates issued under the corporate seal; (3) The registered office of the Company is established at [Street address], Alberta, and the Notice of Registered Office is approved for filing with the Alberta Registrar of Corporations; (4) The following officers are appointed: [President], [Corporate Secretary], [Chief Financial Officer], each with standard signing authority; (5) Banking instruments, the corporate seal, bylaws, and annual statutory filings are ratified. The directors are authorized to take all actions required to effect incorporation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; NUANS-accredited corporate search provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name (e.g., [Company Name] Commercial Inspection and Testing Corp.) to a NUANS-accredited search house; obtain a NUANS report dated within 90 days of filing; either reserve the name via the Registry or proceed to incorporation under the reserved exact name; use a numbered company if no name clearance is sought.
required_dossiers: NUANS Search Request Form
Proposed corporate name and legal element (Inc./Corp.)
Authorization letter from the proposed incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report identifies a confusingly similar existing name, choose an alternate distinctive name or add a geographic/industry qualifier, obtain a fresh NUANS report, and re-file; no refund applies but the revised search is issued within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (RegistryXPRESS / online or paper counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate name, registered office in Alberta, share structure (voting common shares and any class rights), directors, and statements permitted by ABCA; attach each director's signed Consent to Act; remit the prescribed government fee (approx. CAD 200 online / CAD 250 paper); submit through the Alberta Corporate Registry portal.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation
NUANS report dated within 90 days
Signed Consent to Act as Director for each initial director
Identification documents of incorporator/directors as required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry objects to the filing, correct the cited provisions and re-submit within the 90-day NUANS validity window; if the name is refused under ABCA s. 12, file amended articles under a cleared alternate name or seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Initial Registry Recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registry verification, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation with the Alberta incorporation file number; confirm that initial registered office and director names appear on the registry record; download certified copies for banking, licensing, and CRA registration; if the registered office was not stated in the Articles, file the Notice of Registered Office.
required_dossiers: Registered copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Incorporation
Initial director list and officer designation
Notice of Registered Office (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is issued with ministerial or typographical errors, apply for a certificate of correction under ABCA; if issuance is delayed beyond the service standard, escalate to Corporate Registry client services; any registry query is cured by filing supplementary information through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Meeting and Statutory Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate registered office (internal governance); Alberta Corporate Registry for recordal only
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by waiver of notice; pass the pro-forma First Board Resolution accepting share subscriptions; adopt Bylaw No. 1; confirm the registered office address; appoint the President, Corporate Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer; approve corporate seal, bank account mandates, and initiation of municipal and industry licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Waiver of Board Meeting Notice or signed meeting minutes
Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Bylaw No. 1
Share subscription agreements, share ledger, and certificates
Consent to Act as Officer forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer resigns before the meeting, obtain a replacement Consent and re-run the appointment; if the registered office changes, file the Notice of Registered Office within 30 days; resolutions can be ratified retroactively by ordinary board resolution if an omission is identified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Consolidation of Statutory Corporate Records, Minute Book, and Banking Mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the corporation; Alberta Corporate Registry oversight if filings later required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Compile the statutory minute book at the registered office: copy of Articles, Certificate of Incorporation, all consents, share register, director and officer registers, Bylaw No. 1, and first board minutes; affix the corporate seal; complete bank mandate forms for opening an operational account accepting Wire Transfer and Wise rails; confirm the registered office is a real physical address in Alberta accessible for process service.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and corporate seal
Certificate of Incorporation and Articles
Share register, director register, and officer register
Bank mandate and authorized signatory list
Registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate records are queried, produce the missing consents or rectifying resolutions ratified by the board; if the registered office is not a verifiable service address, retain a registered agent and file the corresponding notice of change.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Standards Council of Canada (SCC) and Canadian Association for Laboratory Accreditation (CALA), with municipal business licensing administered by the relevant Alberta municipality (e.g., City of Calgary, City of Edmonton); Alberta Labour and Immigration for occupational safety
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ISO/IEC 17020 Inspection Body Accreditation (factory inspection and quality control agency) or ISO/IEC 17025 Testing Laboratory Accreditation issued by SCC/CALA; municipal Business Licence for commercial inspection office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) in coordination with Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Registration tier under the Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act; on-site inspection-only operations are normally Exempt from full EIA registration because no stationary emissions are generated; an EPEA Registration and Waste Registration become mandatory only if an in-house laboratory or fixed discharge point is opened
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: municipal sewer limits typically pH 6.0-9.5, BOD below 300 mg/L, total suspended solids below 350 mg/L; volatile organic compound emissions at or below Alberta Code of Practice thresholds under CEPA; hazardous waste handling and manifests under the Alberta EPEA Waste Regulation and Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG) requirements if sample waste is transported

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate under the Alberta Fire Code and municipal fire marshal approval; professional engineer structural load inspection for any fixed laboratory/QC equipment; Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) program clearance including WHMIS/GHS chemical safety training and site-specific emergency response plan

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); GST/HST and corporate tax administration portal: CRA My Business Account via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; provincial corporate registry counterpart: Alberta Corporate Registry (https://www.albertaca.com).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta Business Corporation is incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and receives an Alberta Corporate Access (ACA) number; it must then obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and program accounts from the CRA by filing Form RC1 or registering online through Business Registration Online (BRO). The BN plus the RT suffix constitutes the GST/HST account; separate RP (payroll), RM (import/export), and RC (corporation income tax) program accounts are opened where applicable. Non-resident corporations must also file Form RC1JA (Request for a Business Number and Registration of Non-Resident) and, if carrying on business in Alberta, an extra-provincial registration with Alberta Corporate Registry. Mandatory attachments include: certificate of incorporation or amalgamation, registered office address, summary of intended Canadian commercial activity (quality-control inspection and testing for export goods), anticipated first taxable supply date, expected Canadian annual gross revenue, and identification of directors and Canadian agent for service of process. CRA issues the BN instantly online and by mail within 10 business days; GST/HST registration is effective on the date chosen or the date of first supply, whichever is earlier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian-incorporated business corporation is deemed resident in Canada under Income Tax Act (Canada) s. 250(4)(a) and taxed at the entity level under Part I on worldwide income; no pass-through or partnership look-through treatment is available for a corporation. Alberta provincial corporate income tax at 8% general rate; federal rate 15% (combined 23% general); a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) is eligible for the federal small business deduction (9%) and Alberta small business rate (2%) on the first C$500,000 of active business income, resulting in combined 11% small-business rate. Non-resident shareholders of the Alberta corporation are subject to Part XIII withholding tax on dividends (generally 25%, reduced to 5-15% under tax treaties). The foreign-parent corporation itself is generally not taxable in Canada on the active export-service income of its Canadian subsidiary except under the treaty permanent-establishment threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or classification election exists under Canadian tax law; a Business Corporation is automatically a separate taxable entity. Applicable elections for this corporation include: (i) ITA s. 85 rollover election on the transfer of eligible property into the corporation at agreed tax values; (ii) ITA s. 87 amalgamation continuity election if the corporation is continued in an amalgamation; (iii) ITA s. 249 election for a non-calendar taxation year; (iv) GST/HST annual or 2-filing election options under ETA ss. 243-247; (v) the hybrid-mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.4-18.6) are mandatory and provide no elective relief. CCPC status is statutory, not elective, and is terminated automatically if the entity fails the qualifying test.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST); Alberta is a non-participating province and applies only the federal GST at 5% with no provincial sales or use tax component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (other than zero-rated supplies) made by the entity in any single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; once a non-resident or domestic corporation exceeds C$30,000, GST/HST registration and the 5% GST collection obligation become mandatory. Cross-border services to non-residents that are zero-rated do not count toward the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No Canadian federal real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate exists; Alberta does not impose any e-invoicing obligation. The CRA mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns (GST/HST NETFILE or CRA Business Gateway API) for registrants with annual taxable supplies above C$1,000,000; e-invoices are permissible, and the CRA Business Gateway API supports machine-to-machine submission. Standard tax invoices must contain the vendor's BN, invoice date, recipient name, description, consideration, and GST payable (ETA s. 224(3)). Quebec's B2B e-invoicing and QR-code mandate (effective September 2026) does not apply in Alberta.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported tangible goods are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 1 where delivered to a non-resident and removed from Canada within 60 days. Services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated under s. 7 of Part V unless performed in Canada in connection with real property in Canada or with goods situated in Canada at the time of performance. For an on-site factory pre-shipment QC and audit agency in Alberta, inspection and testing performed on goods physically present on an Alberta factory floor at the time of testing are excluded from zero-rating and attract 5% GST even when billed to a foreign buyer. Zero-rating is available where the goods are in Canada solely for the purpose of the QC or testing and are then exported (goods-in-transit or CRA policy), or where the service is performed at a foreign plant. The Canadian exporter of the inspected goods can zero-rate its goods sale and claim input tax credits for the QC service fee, provided the export documents are retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Canadian Export Declaration, B13A format, or CADEX/EDI record) filed by the exporter or licensed customs broker
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing removal of the goods from Canada to a foreign consignee
Commercial Invoice and Certificate of Inspection endorsed by the QC agency and signed by the foreign buyer or principal
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or Wise transaction record evidencing settlement by the non-resident principal in foreign currency
Written inspection contract between the non-resident principal and the QC agency stating that the service is performed for the non-resident outside its Canadian business activity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada does not impose a specific 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation statute; the 180-day benchmark is retained by the compliance pipeline as an internal evidentiary cutoff for export substantiation. CRA audit practice requires documentary retention for at least six years from the end of the taxation year. Where zero-rating is improperly claimed and export proof is missing, CRA will reassess the supply as taxable at 5% and charge interest at the prescribed rate plus the late-remittance penalty (ETA s. 280: 5% of the unremitted amount plus 1% per month up to 12 months); false or deceptive statements triggering gross negligence attract an additional 50% penalty under ETA s. 285 and ITA s. 163(2). Fraudulent export schemes are criminal offences under ETA s. 330 and ITA s. 239, with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years; civil clawbacks run retrospectively to the date of the original zero-rating claim, and input tax credits are correspondingly denied where the QC agency fails to substantiate its own commercial activity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary and systemic stability authority); financial-sector AML supervision by FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada); banking conduct, solvency, and prudential regulation by OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. There are no statutory exchange controls, conversion queues, approval requirements, or profit repatriation hurdles for dividends, service fees, capital returns, or liquidation proceeds. All cross-border transactions remain subject only to general AML, sanction screening, FATCA/CRS reporting, and OSFI/FINTRAC transaction-reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain revenue in any permissible currency, hold foreign-currency bank accounts at Canadian financial institutions, and settle invoices in Canadian dollars without restriction. Receipts at or above CAD 10,000, and any wire transfer forming part of a reportable cross-border transaction, must be reported to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability with material legal constraints. Wise (Wise Canada Inc.) and similar firms operate in Canada as FINTRAC-registered money services businesses, not as electronic money institutions as recognised in the EU/UK. Such fintechs cannot accept deposits, issue e-money, provide Canadian Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) protection, or extend regulated bank credit. They are usable only for low-value cross-border supplier disbursements, minor FX conversion, and expense payments. Treasury-grade escrow, trade finance, and liquidity clearing must be held through a Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is generally required for at least one director or senior officer at a Schedule I bank branch, or remote onboarding through a bank-governed video interview with notarized and apostilled identity documents. Fully self-service remote opening is unavailable for first-time non-resident-owned private corporations. All directors and all beneficial owners with a direct or indirect stake exceeding 25% must provide original or certified identity records. The interview may be waived only where the corporation already maintains an existing banking relationship with the same lending institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain includes high-risk, opaque, or FATF-grey-listed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Alberta corporate registry extract; full organizational chart showing every direct and indirect ownership node above 10%; passport and residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; audited financial statements or notarized balance sheet; independent trade counterparty references; and a jurisdictional rationale memorandum explaining commercial substance in each involved country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of funds for capital injection, escrow funding, or intercompany inflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of sending-bank statements; underlying commercial contract or equity subscription agreement that triggers the wire; corporate and personal tax filings demonstrating lawful earnings; no-cash-use declaration; confirmation that all funds derive from banking wires or invoices traceable to the inspection agency business; and an attorney or banker reference letter verifying the sending entity's identity and regulatory standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound-outbound payment flow inconsistent with a low-risk factory inspection agency profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client engagement agreement for pre-shipment quality control; dated factory inspection report and photographic evidence; commercial invoice and QC certificate; supplier or subcontractor agreement; third-party laboratory or calibration certificate; bill of lading or logistics record; and a cash-flow forecast memo that reconciles each wire to the corresponding trade disbursement, including SWIFT purpose codes and order numbers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the Schedule I bank account, denominated in CAD or USD, with the OECD BPM6 purpose code for direct investment equity injection between affiliated enterprises. Each wire must be accompanied by the sending bank's ABA and sort code, the Alberta entity's institution number and transit number, a pre-submitted corporate authorization form, and the intercompany equity or shareholder loan agreement. Any wire above CAD 100,000 is likely to be paused by the receiving bank until the KYC Fircosoft and Canadian sanctions screens are cleared and the documentation file is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 direct beneficiary payments or documentary commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 by the Canadian bank's trade finance desk. CAD high-value payments settle through Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS); USD payments settle via correspondent bank networks, principally CHIPS or Fedwire. Low-value operational disbursements may be made through Wise or another FINTRAC-registered MSB, but such rails must never be used for capital repatriation, escrow release, or documentary LC obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards with OSFI-regulated bank counterparties
FX swaps for short-term cross-currency liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps for long-term intercompany and capex hedging
FX options with physical delivery or cash settlement, restricted to corporate hedging rather than speculation
Natural hedging through multicurrency operating accounts and CAD/USD cash pooling
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for illiquid or prohibited-currency exposures, and only through an OSFI-licensed dealer confirmed to have no CAD/USD NDF market reliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return under ABCA s. 114 (confirms registered office, directors, and articles data; fee CAD 45 online / CAD 60 paper, approx. USD 33/44 at 0.74 CAD/USD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (filed through an authorized corporate registry service provider)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 (approx. USD 74) late fee on any return filed after the 60-day window; if returns are un-filed for at least one year, the Registrar may serve statutory notice and administratively dissolve the corporation under ABCA s. 212 without court order; revival under s. 209 requires all overdue returns, fees and late fees to be settled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of shareholders (or unanimous resolution in lieu) with signed minutes entered into the Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and corporate Minute Book retained at the Alberta registered office (no external registry filing required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; each later AGM within 15 months of the preceding AGM; may be replaced by a unanimous shareholder resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty; a shareholder or director may petition the Court under ABCA s. 128 to compel a meeting, and prolonged failure to hold AGMs exposes directors to resolution for appointment or removal by court order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal Part I plus Alberta corporate tax administered by CRA under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; corporate balance due 2 months after fiscal year-end (3 months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under ITA s. 162(1): 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, with an additional 10% on a second offence; CRA interest accrues daily; directors of a private inspection agency are not personally liable for unpaid corporate income tax absent special circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual or quarterly return for taxable inspection/quality-control services (registrant once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within 3 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly filers: within 1 month after each calendar quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ETA s. 280 penalty of 5% of the unremitted net tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, compounding interest on arrears; continued failure can trigger higher penalties on repeat occasions and gross-negligence penalties where intentional.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 payroll information returns (employee statements and employer summary) with annual payroll reconciliation, where employees are engaged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T4 Summary due by the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ITA s. 162(5) penalties per late T4 statement plus separate penalties for the T4 Summary; unremitted source deductions (CPP, EI, income tax) attract interest, penalties and potential director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold forces an audit for a private Alberta non-distributing corporation. Under ABCA ss. 155-156, an auditor is mandatory only for distributing (public-market) corporations; a private inspection/QC agency may waive the auditor annually by unanimous shareholder resolution, but any single shareholder can demand an audit as at the most recent AGM.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS applicable to publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may elect ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II); both IFRS and ASPE constitute acceptable GAAP for CRA and Alberta corporate income tax.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta's ABCA annual return does not currently require a beneficial-ownership (UBO/ISC) declaration for private corporations; no annual confirmation of shareholding transfers is made in the registry filing. Share transfers are recorded contemporaneously by board resolution, share certificate cancellation and Register of Members entry, with the resulting director list shown on the next annual return. The CBCA individuals-with-significant-control register applies only to federal corporations; Alberta ISC-registry amendments should be monitored for future proclamation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing articles, by-laws, board and shareholder minutes, and unanimous shareholder agreements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 120–600 per year (approx. USD 90–445 at 0.74 CAD/USD) including registered office address, annual return handling and agent services; mail forwarding and director service add CAD 50–300.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 3,000–14,000 (approx. USD 2,200–10,400) for a full statutory audit of a small inspection/QC agency; CAD 1,200–4,000 (approx. USD 900–3,000) for a review engagement where shareholders waive the audit.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined federal+Alberta general corporate rate (federal 15% + Alberta 8%); 11.0% combined CCPC small business rate (federal 9% + Alberta 2%) on first CAD 500,000 active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction (first CAD 500,000 active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations); SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable credit for CCPCs on qualifying expenditures); Alberta innovation and investment tax credits; accelerated and full-expensing CCA classes for manufacturing/testing equipment (e.g., Class 43/44/53)
